name: compress-gzip
algorithm: Gzip a 50 MB log text with the std's compressor at its default level, rounds times; the checksum adds every input byte and the input length per round, so it is the same for every compressor (compressed sizes go to stderr).

skip.c: no std gzip in C (zlib is not std)
skip.rust: no std gzip in Rust (flate2 is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the round trip is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestSTDCOMPRESS_GoReadsMkOutput), and the compressed sizes are printed for the ratio column
notes: The input is the regex row's log text (tools/bench gen kind log, seed 5; 50,000,038 bytes). Bytes per second = 50,000,038 * rounds / median.

Each side runs its std's default level, which is a different algorithm in each: Mk's std.compress.Gzip has one level, the matcher of Go 1.27's level 6 (fastEncL6: a 4-byte and a 7-byte hash table, no chains) with Mk's block writer; Go's compress/gzip at gzip.DefaultCompression runs fastEncL6; Zig's std.compress.flate.Compress at Options.default runs zlib's level 6 (lazy matching over hash chains, chain 128). The compressed sizes on stderr are the ratio column: on the owner's machine (std-compress session 2, not a published number) Mk 11,901,522 bytes, Go 11,914,127, Zig 11,768,138.

Allocation per round, made alike (SC-2): every column makes its output buffer and compressor state once, before the loop, where its API allows. Go: one bytes.Buffer grown once to the Zig buffer's size and one gzip.Writer, Reset onto it each round. Zig: one output buffer under a fixed std.Io.Writer, a Compress (a stack value) per round over one window buffer. Mk: one arena made before the loop and Reset each round; Gzip takes its output (the stored-form bound, zero filled by Arena.Slice) from it, and Reset returns a chunk of over 512 KiB to the heap, so that output is a fresh heap allocation each round, and its 448 KiB of scratch is a sub-arena it makes and frees: those costs are Mk's API and are counted against Mk.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
